notes: Summary: Lakeview (global fintech, 1200+ engs) evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing AI assistants and high-throughput reranking in production.

Primary ask: deterministic throughput guarantees across business hours, 99th percentile latency SLOs (P99 target < 150ms for short chat responses, < 250ms for multi-doc rerank), and explicit failover headroom in multi-region pools.
Current infra: mix of in-house GPU clusters for batch and managed endpoints for experiments. Want to avoid developing heavy routing layer; prefer Redwood smart-routing + reserved pools.
Regional footprint requested: primary pools in us-east-1 and us-west-2, warm standby in eu-west-1 for EU traffic residency and failover. Also mention AZ-spread within regions (min 2 AZs per region).

Sizing proposal (customer-suggested during scoping call): baseline 32x H100-equivalent GPUs (16 per primary region) + 20% failover headroom (reserve additional 8 GPUs), ability to burst + autoscale to 48 GPUs across pool for peak events.

Throughput targets: sustained 400 qps of short chat (avg 30 token responses) per region during peak; reranking workload requires 200 qps with tight p99 latency. Want capacity reserved for 95% of peak traffic and autoscale/burst for remainder.

Demand pattern: predictable business hours (08:00-20:00 local), weekly traffic spikes at end-of-month and quarterly product launches. Interested in committed weekly throughput windows with associated unit pricing.

POC plan: 2-week guarded production POC. Week 1 - run production shadow traffic on dedicated pool for chat, measure p50/p95/p99; Week 2 - run rerank benchmark with synthetic peak and do failover drill between us-east and us-west.

SLA negotiation points raised by customer: credits for missed throughput or p99 latency violations, definition of "available" GPUs versus synchronized KV caches for session continuity, cross-region RTO goal (<=5 minutes for routing failover).

Security/compliance notes: must pass internal security review (SOC2 required), KMS integration needed for model prompt logging encryption, EU data residency requirement for subset of traffic—customer wants optional Private deployment for EU region or dedicated VPC tenancy.
Quote from CPO during demo: "We cannot accept opaque failover behaviour — we need explicit headroom and runbook for cross-region cutover."

Procurement: procurement team prefers 12-month committed capacity contract with quarterly review of utilization and rightsizing adjustments. Finance asked for ARR band estimate and overage pricing cap.

Technical questions outstanding: how KV cache syncing works cross-region, cost model for burst capacity vs committed reserve, whether autoscaling can be constrained by AZ-level pool sizing, and observed p99 under mixed chat+rerank workloads.

Internal Redwood notes: SE to produce two capacity layouts (conservative and aggressive) — include GPU SKU mapping (A100/H100 equivalence), expected tokens/sec, and cost delta. AE/Jordan to push draft SLA to legal by 2025-02-10. SE Priya to schedule POC kickoff 2025-02-12.
Attachments referenced: capacity-layout-v1.xlsx (in drive), POC-runbook-template.md, security-answers-lakeview.pdf.
